summary: The document concludes that despite ongoing studies like those by the Edison Electric Institute, the uncertainties of rate redesign effects, consumer response time lags, and long construction lead times mean that conservation and rate revision cannot serve as reasonable alternatives to the Bad Creek Project at this time.
text: While improved conservation measures such as redesign of rates should be pursued vigorously, the uncertainties of the effects of specific rate redesigns and other conservation measures on the load characteristics of an electric system, the time lag associated with consumer responses, and the long times required for constructing new capacity, severely reduce the practical potential of rate revision and conservation as alternatives, at this time, to the scheduling of projected needed additional generating capacity. Accordingly, these measures cannot be considered as reasonable alternatives to the proposed Bad Creek Project.
